To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the $\epsilon$-projection is a generalization of the projection, that the $\epsilon-$subgradient is a generalization and a unifying framework of the subgradient, and that the $\epsilon -$subgradient method is a generalization as well as a unifying framework to many existing methods for convex optimization.
the incremental subgradients can be used to solve the convex feasibility problem and that the resulting algorithms have the potential of solving large-scale constrained convex optimization problems.

(1) the incremental subgradient method is a special case of an algorithm for the convex feasibility problems, (2) the incremental subgradients method can be extended to the case of a non-smooth convex objective function, (3) the incremental subgradents method can be extended for the case when the feasible set is defined by a system of linear inequalities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
incremental methods for constrained convex optimization.
the development of new methods and theoretical analysis of existing methods in the context of large-scale constrained convex optimization.
developing new incremental subgradient methods for constrained optimization problems and applying them to large-scale problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new methods are more robust, more efficient, and easier to implement than their predecessors.
the new algorithms proposed here are very competitive and can be used in many applications.
we have developed a unifying framework that brings together $\epsilon$ subgradient methods and methods for the constrained convex feasibility problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how to use approximate projections in $\epsilon$- subgradient algorithms to solve constrained optimization problems.
we present a unifying approach for nonsmooth optimization, bringing together the two major classes of algorithms, namely, the $\epsilon$- subgradient method and the method of alternating projections.
we provide a new framework for constrained convex optimization, and that the resulting incremental subgradients methods are suitable for large-scale convex optimization problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the $\epsilon$-projection step is a key element in designing new methods for nonsmooth optimization.
incremental methods can be used in a unified way for solving constrained convex optimization problems.
$\epsilon$-proximity operators can be used to approximate projections onto closed convex sets and, as a consequence, to construct new algorithms for constrained nonsmooth optimization.
